The patient has a history of Sickle Cell Anemia (Hb SS), which was diagnosed at birth. The diagnosis of SCD was confirmed at 3 months of age. The patient has been on chronic blood transfusion for 3 years, which led to iron overload due to non-compliance with chelation therapy. The patient has a history of massive lymph node enlargement and vaso-occlusive crisis.

The 36-year-old African American female patient was admitted to our hospital with persistent fatigue at the age of 35. CBC test showed leukocytes = 3270/µL, hemoglobin = 9.3 g/dL, hematocrit = 26.9%, mean corpuscular volume = 91.5 fL, platelet count = 252,000/µL, and absolute neutrophil count = 1,260/µL. Subsequent complete blood count tests showed anemia which required red blood cell (RBC) transfusions.

The patient, a 6-month-old entire male Hungarian Viszla, presented with well-demarcated, ulcerative and exudative skin lesions, smaller lesions of similar appearance on the left thoracic paw and multiple small ulcers on the tongue. Abnormal results from SNAP cPLi test (quantitative value > 2000 μg/L; consistent with pancreatitis).

Although bilirubin and transaminase both improved after interruption of anti-TB treatment for 10 days (AST: 61 IU/L; ALT: 38 IU/L; total bilirubin: 1.72 mg/dL; and direct bilirubin: 1.37 mg/dL), the general condition of the patient deteriorated gradually.
The patient presented with recurrent severe anemia requiring multiple blood transfusions.
Serological tests confirmed the diagnosis of infectious mononucleosis. Serological tests for hepatitis A, B, C, CMV, HIV, and Toxoplasma Gondi were negative.

Initial evaluation included iron studies, chest X-ray, abdominal ultrasound, and serum erythropoietin. JAK2 V617F and exon 12 mutations were negative. A bone marrow biopsy revealed a mild increase in erythropoiesis, but was otherwise normal.

query: 原因 of Troponin I elevation
pos: The patient presented to the ER with chest pain after learning about her mother's death, which was mainly retrosternal and continuous. An EKG obtained showed T-wave inversions and positive Troponin I.
negs: The serum alpha-1-fetoprotein measured 17,400 ng/mL initially, and 15,000 ng/mL two months later during the follow-up.
Subsequently, the patient was started on a heparin infusion. He had two serial troponins obtained, which were within normal limits.

Initial tests showed a normal 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) and normal troponin I levels. However, three hours later, the laboratory high-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn) T was found to be elevated. The patient had atypical non-ischemic changes in his repeat ECG, and emergency transthoracic echocardiography showed a small volume of pericardial effusion.

The patient was admitted with severe aortic stenosis and a history of hypertension and percutaneous coronary intervention to the left anterior descending artery. Transthoracic echocardiography showed a peak gradient of 80 mmHg and mean gradient of 45 mmHg across the calcified aortic valve.

The patient presented to the Emergency Department (ED) with a one-week history of ankle swelling and abdominal pain. Laboratory tests showed leukocytosis with neutrophilia, mild anemia, high calcium levels, mildly elevated liver enzyme levels and elevated NT-proBNP and procalcitonin levels.
IC nitroglycerin was administered resulting in the resolution of the spasm and ST-elevation. The patient was started on IV nitroglycerin which was later changed to isosorbide mononitrate.
The diagnosis of ICI-induced MG was made. Anti-striational antibodies were found to be positive with an elevated titer of 1:80.
Laboratory findings revealed elevated levels of ALT and AST with no change in serum HBV, but HBV DNA was found to be significantly increased. The tumor marker CA125 was also elevated.
